full_judgment:
Farid Ahmed J : This Rule Nisi was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the acquisition proceeding in LA Case No. 8 of 1992 by the Land Acquisition Officer, Comilla, acquiring the petitioner's land measuring 0.20 acres being Dag No. 647 Khatian No. 312. Mouza-Homna J L No. 51. Thana Homna, District-Comilla, should not be declared to have been passed without any lawful authority and to be of no legal effect and or such other or further order or orders passed as to this court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The facts as stated in the petition are that the petitioner is the owner of the homestead land measuring 0.20 acres where he was living with his family members and also has been running a tea stall in the small part of it. He filled up a ditch of about 25 x 30 feet by collecting earth from various places and erected two houses of 24' x 12' and 44' x 12' as corrugated tinshed. The covetous eyes of an influential mighty person of the society fell on the said land who made an offer to purchase the same at a consideration of Taka 10 lac and having failed he forcibly hanged a signboard of the then ruling party. The petitioner then removed the signboard from his land. On 29-7-90 a meeting of Upazila Parishad under the Chairmanship of the then Upazila Chairman Mr. Amzad Hossain was held and in the said meeting a resolution was adopted to the effect that 0.20 acres land of plot No.647 is required for expansion of Homna Upazila Complex. As per said resolution the then Upazila Nirbahi Officer (UNO) prepared a specific proforma for the requisition and acquisition of the property and the same was sent to the Land Acquisition Officer, Comilla, who started LA Case No.8 of 1992-93 for the acquisition of the land in question. On 12-12-92 a notice under section 3 of the Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Ordinance, 1982 was issued in favour of the petitioner asking him to submit objection, if any against the said proposal for acquisition. The petitioner submitted his objection on 29-12-92 and on 7-2-93 his objection was rejected. The authority found that the property is required for public purpose and for public interest and sent the proposal to the Divisional Commissioner for approval. Thereafter notice under section 6(I)(3) of the Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Ordinance, was served upon the petitioner vide Memo dated 19-6-93 duly signed by the Deputy Commissioner. Finding no other alternative, the petitioner instituted Title Suit No. 16 of 1993 in the Court of Assistant Judge. Homna, Comilla, for declaration that the acquisition of the land of the petitioner is null and void and that the same is malafide, and not for public purpose or public interest. 

 3. The respondents have contested the suit by filing written statements alleging that the acquisition is for bona fide public purpose for the public interest. The learned Assistant Judge on 26-8-96 decreed the suit. 

 4. Against the said judgment and decree of the trial Court, the respondents preferred Title Appeal No. 219 of 1996 before the learned District Judge Comilla and the learned Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Comilla by Judgment and decree dated 31-1-02 allowed the appeal and dismissed the suit holding that the suit challenging the proceeding started under the Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Ordinance. 1082 was not maintainable. 

 5. By tiling two separate supplementary affidavits dated 1-3-06 and 15-3-06 the petitioner has also contended that though the requiring body i.e. Thana Nirbahi Officer (TNO), gave their proposal to acquire the land in question to protect the Upazila Parishad Bhaban and administrative sanction was also given for the said purpose by the Ministry of Local Government Rural Development and Co-operatives but the notice under section 3 of the Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Ordinance, 1982, signed by the Land Acquisition Officer was issued mentioning that the property is needed or likely to be needed to expand the Homna Thana Parishad. The petitioner also stated that the local administration and the land acquisition authority have proceeded to acquire the land of the petitioner in question under the pressure and to meet the sweet will of a Cabinet Secretary who thereafter became the Commerce Minister, thereafter the Minister or Waster Transport of the then Government and thereafter the Minister of Industry or the present Government, whose proposal of buying the said homestead land was not accepted by the petitioner and that the said facts would be evidenced from the letter dated 21-4-92 issued by the Ministry of Local Government. Rural Development and Co-operatives to the Upazila Nirbani Officer, Homna, according administrative approval for the acquisition of the property (Annexure-F) and from the letter dated 16-9-93 (Annexure-H) issued by the TNO to the Deputy Commissioner, Comilla for receiving fund for compensation against acquisition and to deliver physical possession of the land, copy of the said letters were served upon the Private Secretary to the then Minister of Commerce and thereafter Private Secretary to the Minister of Water Transport, though the said Ministry is not the concerned Ministry for requisition and acquisition of the property. The petitioner also stated that there are vast vacant Government high lands available in front side and in the east and west side of the Upazila Bhaban, the proposal for acquisition of the petitioner's land for the expansion of the Upazila Parish ad Bhaban is malafide, unjustified and not reasonable. The said acquisition proceedings have not been finalised and a declaration of the acquisition of the property by the Deputy Commissioner has yet not been published in the Official Gazette. The property in question is still vacant and no building or foundation for construction was undertaken in the said land, except a boundary wall in the north end of the land was constructed in the year 2003 after issuance of the Rule by this Court. 

 7. The petitioner, being aggrieved by the acquisition proceedings under I-A case No. 6 of 1991-92 started by the respondents has preferred the writ petition and obtained the instant Rule. 

 8. Mr AKM Fazlul Hoque, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner, submits that the reason for the acquisition of the property must have been stated definitely and specifically. When the requiring body needs the property for one reason and the property is acquired or notified to be acquired for another reason, it is a sign of arbitrary and whimsical use of statutory power by the authority and therefore, the notice under section 3 of the Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Ordinance, 1982 and the proceedings for acquisition is liable to be declared as unlawful and without any jurisdiction. Mr Fazlul Hoque also submits that in the notice under section 3 of the Ordinance it has been mentioned that the property is needed or likely to be needed for the public purpose whereby it has been kept open for both the alternatives, though the law requires that the Deputy Commissioner will have to choose one, and, as such, the acquisition proceedings should be declared as illegal and without lawful authority, Mr Fazlul Hoque thereafter submits that keeping vast land unused within the campus of the Upazila complex, the purpose of acquisition is malafide and for private interest to meet the sweet will of an influential person and not for the bonafide  public interest or public purpose and, as such, the Rule is liable to be made absolute. 

 9. Mr Zaman Akhter, the learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing on behalf of the respondents, without tiling any affidavit-in-opposition, submits that the land in question is required for the expansion of Upazila Parishad for the public interest and the acquiring authority after observing all formalities as required under the Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Ordinance, 1982, acquired the property, the objection of the petitioner made under section 4(1) of the Ordinance, was considered by the Divisional Commissioner and found that the property proposed to be acquired for the public purpose for the expansion of Upazila Parishad, the land in question is necessary and, as such, it cannot be said that the proceedings for acquisition of the property is a malafide action and the same is not for public purpose and, as such, the Rule is liable to be discharged. 

 10. It appears from Annexure-E that a proforma (proposal for acquisition was filled up by the TNO on 9-9-92 and stated that the said 0.20 acres land which is a ditch is required for the protection of the Homna Parishad Bhaban and that by filing up the said land, the main Upazila Parishad Bhaban would be protected. Annexure-F, a letter dated 21-4-92 issued by the Assistant Secretary, Ministry of Local Government, Rural Development and Co-operatives intimating the TNO Homna Upazila, Comilla, that administrative approval was given for the acquisition of the land in question to protect the building of the Upazila Parishad Bhaban. Annexure-G is the notice dated 12-1-92 under section 3 of the Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Ordinance 1982 hereinafter referred to as the Ordinance issued by the Land Acquisition Officer Comilla, wherein it has been mentioned that the land in question is required to be acquired for the public purpose for the expansion of Hornna Upazila Parishad Bhaban and the said land is required. and likely to be required for acquisition and asked the petitioner to file objection, if any, within 15 days from the date of receipt of the said notice. The notice issued under section 3 of the Ordinance reads as follows: 

 11. From the contents of the said notice it appears that the land was proposed to be acquired for the expansion of the Hornna Upazila Parishad for the public purpose which is required or likely to be required for the said purpose and by this notice it has been kept open for both the alternatives, though the law requires that the Deputy Commissioner will have to choose one and in the said notice the purpose tor acquisition shall have to be specifically mentioned. It also appears from the said notice that the Land Acquisition Officer signed the notice 12-12-92 though under section 3 of the said Ordinance it is the Deputy Commissioner who has to cause a notice to be published under the said Ordinance. 

 12. The learned Deputy Attorney-General has failed to satisfy us from the record that the' Deputy Commissioner authorised the land acquisition officer to issue such letter or the law empower, that Land Acquisition Officer to issue such letter Under the provisions of section 3 of the Ordinance the Deputy Commissioner has to say whether the property in question is needed or alternatively whether it is likely to be needed but he cannot say at the same time that it is both needed or likely to be needed. On considering the notice under section 3 of the Ordinance (Annexure-G) we find that the same was not issued for any specific purpose and the same has not been issued by a proper authority i.e. the Deputy Commissioner who is authorised by law to issue such letter. The learned Advocate for the petitioner has cited the case of Sankar Gopal Chatterjee vs Additional Commissioner. Dhaka Division reported in 41 DLR 326 and the case of Abdul Kader vs Masaddar Ali reported in 3 BLC (AD) 211. In the case reported in 41 DLR 326 it has been held. 

 13. This view of the High Court Division has been approved by our Appellate Division in the case reported in 3 BLC (AD) 21. After the issuance of the notice under section 6 of the Ordinance, the petitioner instituted Title Suit No. 16 of 1993 in the Court of learned Assistant Judge, Homna, Com ilia, for declaration that the acquisition proceeding is illegal, malafide and the same is without jurisdiction. The learned Assistant Judge decreed the suit by judgment and decree dated 20-8-96 declaring that the acquisition of property is mala tide and not for public purpose. 

 14. The respondents against the said judgment and decree of the trial Court preferred Title Appeal No. 219 before the learned District Judge, Comilla. The learned Joint District Judge 3rd Court Comilla by judgment and decree dated 31-1-02 allowed the appeal holding that the suit is barred under section 44 of the Ordinance and that the proceeding initiated under the Acquisition and Requisition of Immovable Property Act cannot be called in question before any Civil Court. 

 15. The petitioner has annexed a sketch map as Annexure-'Ll' along with his supplementary affidavit dated 15-3-06. In the said sketch map it has been shown that the Upazila Complex is situated adjacent to big public road from two sides i.e. from the east and the west 7-8 feet wide public roads have connected the Upazila Complex with the main road and around the said two connected roads there are available vacant lands of the Upazila Parishad. It also appears from the said sketch map that a big vacant land is lying in front of the Upazila Parishad Bhaban, The area of the said land according to the petitioner is about one acre. In the northern side of the Upazila Bhaban the proposed land for acquisition is situated. From the sketch map, we find that the extension of Upazila Parishad can be easily done in the vacant land of the Upazila Parishad. The respondents have mentioned in their proposal for acquisition that the lands is required for the protection of the building and in the notice under section 3 it has been mentioned that for the extension of the Upazila Parishad, the land is required or likely to be required. So, we find that respondents are not sure or definite about their purpose for the acquisition of the property. The proposal was made in the year 1990 for the acquisition of the property till today there is no allegation from the side of the respondents within these 15 years that without the proposed land the protection of the main building or Upazila Parishad is being hampered. It has not been denied by the respondents that there is no available vacant land of the Government south of the Upazila Parishad or within Upazila Complex. The petitioner has asserted that a Cabinet Secretary who thereafter became an influential Minister of the then political party in power tried to purchase the land in question by creating pressure upon the petitioner and having failed he has influenced the acquisition authority to take steps for the acquisition of the property in the name of expansion of the Upazila Parishad Bhaban and to show the involvement of the said influential Minister, the learned Advocate has drawn our attention to Annexures-Il and III which show that copy of the said annexures were forwarded to the Private Secretary of the said Minister, though the said Minister or Ministry has nothing to do on the question of the land in question. This action of the respondents also shows the malafide intention of the respondents in acquiring the property. The petitioner has also made statements on oath annexing some photographs to show the present position of the proposed acquired land and the vacant land situated within the complex of the Upazila Parishad. From the said photographs it seems to us that a vacant land is available in front of the Upazila Parishad. 

 16. From the above discussions, we find that the proposal for acquisition of the land in question was not bonafide and the notice for the acquisition of the property is a mala fide action of the respondents and the same was not for a specific purpose or tor public purpose. The notice under section 3 of the Ordinance, was not issued by a competent officer and, as such, the proceedings of LA Case No. 8 of 1992-93 is declared to be illegal and without lawful authority and the same has got no legal basis. 

 Md Muzammel Hossain J : I respectfully agree with my learned brother in making the Rule absolute Since my learned brother has stated the facts of the case, and the points involved in making the Rule absolute I would like to add a few words of my own and to focus on the intention of the requiring body as a proforma was submitted by the Thana Nirbahi Officer on 9-9-1992 (Annexure-E). On perusal of Annexure E it appears that the purpose of the proposal was to acquire the land in question tor the protection of the Upazila Parishad Bhaban. It also appears from the memo dated 21-4-92 issued by the Ministry of Local Government, Rural Development and Co-operatives (Annexure F) and possession certificate (Annexure 1) issued by the Land Acquisition Officer that the purpose, of the acquisition was for the protection of the Upazila Parishad Bhaban whereas from the notice dated 12-12-1992 under section 3 of the Ordinance (Annexure G) it appears that the land in question is required for the extension of the Upazila Parishad Bhaban. Section 3 of the Acquisition and Requisitions of Immovable Properties Ordinance 1982 empowers the Deputy Commissioner to publish a notice at a convenient place on or near the property which is needed or likely to be needed for any public purpose or in the public interest stating that the property is proposed to be acquired. In the case of Shankar Gopal Chatterjee vs Additional Commissioner; Dhaka Division reported in 41 DLR 326 a Division Bench of this Hon'ble Court held that the Law of Acquisition gives the Deputy Commissioner power to acquire property in two likely situations, Firstly, if the property is needed and secondly, if the property is likely to be needed. A property is either needed or it is likely to be needed, but while acquiring a property the Deputy Commissioner cannot keep both the alternatives in his pocket. He has to choose between the two, if he keeps both the options open, then he does not know whether the property is needed for immediate use or it likely to be needed for some future use. The use of both these alternative expressions in the notice under section 3 is indicative of a lack of application of mind and the notice under section 3 is liable to be struck down on that ground as well. In the case Abdul Quadir vs Masaddar Ali reported in 3 BLC (AD) 211 the Appellate Division held that when the two alternatives are kept open then there was total non-application of mind and the whole exercise by the petitioner was a malafide move to get the land aequired illegally when he himself failed to purchase the same as has been found by the High Court Division. In the instant case since the respondents, requiring authority and acquiring authority, expressed different purpose if cannot be said clearly for which purpose the land in question is going to be acquired. It appears that there is a total non-application of mind on the part of the authority which makes the order liable to be struck down. The petitioner in the; Supplementary-Affidavit stated that there is no precise or definite purpose for the acquisition of the land in question in as much as the respondents purported to acquire the land on the one hand for the protection of the Upazila Parishad Bhaban and on the other hand, for the extension of the Upazila complex. Since the very purpose of the acquisition is ambiguous or otherwise uncertain, the Acquiring Body did not know or does not know for what purpose the land was or is required to be acquired. It has been asserted on behalf of the petitioner that the local administration and the Acquiring Body proceeded to acquire the land in question at the behest of a mighty person who is a former secretary and presently an influential Minister of the Government holding different portfolios and whose proposal of buying the said homestead land was not accepted by the petitioner. The learned Advocate for the petitioner has brought to our notice some other correspondences namely; Memo dated 21-4-1992 (Annexure F), Memo dated 16-9-1992 (Annexure-H), Memo dated 18-11-2000 [ Annexure-H(1)] forwarded to the Private Secretary to the Hon'ble Minister stating the name of the Ministry. There is no rhyme and reason to understand why these memos should be addressed to the Private Secretary to the Hon'ble Minister who was or is not at all involved or in-charge of the Ministry or who is not concerned as to the acquisition of the land under the Acquisition and Requisition of Immoveable Property Ordinance, 1982 and the Rules framed thereunder. From the statements of the petitioner and the sketch map annexed to the Supplementary-Affidavit, it is evident that there is a big vacant land measuring one acre in front of the Upazila Parishad Bhaban. The petitioner asserted that extension of the Upazila Parishad could be easily done in the said vacant land. The petitioner has also asserted that a mighty person being an influential Minister having failed to grab the property, impressed upon the Acquiring Authority to take steps for the acquisition of the property in question. Since these statements of the petitioner have not been controverted by the respondents it is deemed to have been admitted to be true. In that view of the matter. We find that the acquisition proceedings have been started with malafide intention to deprive the petitioner in the absence of any bonafide requirement. Though the proposal for acquisition was made in 1990 yet till today there is no material evidence on record to show that in the absence of the acquisition of the property in question the existence of the Upazila Parishad haban is in jeopardy. It is well established that rnalafide vitiates everything. Malatide has been defined by the Indian Supreme Court in the decision of the case of Jaichand VWD AIR 1967 SC 483 in the following terms: 

 When any action is taken or proceeding is initiated with mala tide intention without formation of any opinion as to the purpose of the acquisition the entire proceedings should be vitiated and, as such, the acquisition proceedings should be declared to be without any lawful authority. For the aforesaid reasons. I also concur with my learned brother in holding that the acquisition proceedings have been made without lawful authority and are of no legal effect. We have also noticed that the respondents Acquiring Authority with malafide intention started the acquisition proceedings in respect of the property in question without any public purpose or without any public interest and, as such, the acquisition proceedings are declared to be without lawful authority. With the aforesaid findings and observations. I concur with my learned brother in making the Rule absolute.
